text: dsh-arrowkey-nav 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的方向键导航插件。它在浏览器文档上注册键盘监听器，读取 DSH 的会话与工作区快照；上、下方向键在当前工作区循环切换会话，左、右方向键按工作区顺序切换。切换后会尝试将目标行滚动到视野中；从空输入框触发时会把焦点送回输入框，有草稿时则保留方向键给光标编辑。插件也会优先复用目标工作区的空白会话或最近更新会话。适合习惯键盘操作、需要快速浏览多个 DSH 会话和工作区的用户。需要安装到 DSH Web profile，并使用声明兼容范围内的 DSH 版本；不需要额外 API 密钥。

dsh-arrowkey-nav adds arrow-key navigation to DSH Web. Up/Down cycle sessions in the current workspace; Left/Right switch workspaces. It scrolls toward the target row and restores focus to an empty composer, while drafts keep their caret keys. No API key is needed.
我想只用键盘在当前工作区的不同会话之间切换。
能不能按工作区顺序快速跳到前一个或后一个工作区？
让会话列表支持用上下键循环浏览，不要跳进其他工作区。
输入框空着时，我希望按方向键就能切换会话。
编辑提示词草稿时怎样避免导航快捷键抢走光标方向键？
切换到别的会话后，能自动把对应的侧边栏行滚动出来吗？
How can I cycle through sessions in the current workspace using only the keyboard?
I want Left and Right to move between workspaces in my DSH web profile.
dsh-arrowkey-nav 的功能「会话导航」：按上、下方向键在当前工作区的可见会话间循环切换；遇到单个会话或没有当前会话时不消费按键。
dsh-arrowkey-nav 的功能「工作区导航」：按左、右方向键遍历工作区；进入目标工作区时优先打开可复用的空白会话，其次选择最近更新的可见会话。
dsh-arrowkey-nav 的功能「编辑时保留方向键」：修饰键、输入法组合、对话框菜单和其他编辑区域会保留自己的按键；输入框有草稿时方向键用于移动光标。
dsh-arrowkey-nav 的功能「定位切换后的会话」：导航后尝试把目标会话行滚动到视野中；如果按键时焦点在空输入框，切换后会将焦点恢复到输入框。
dsh-arrowkey-nav 使用前须知：折叠的工作区分组或侧栏不会挂载目标行，因此切换仍会发生，但滚动定位无法显示目标行（README.md:132-141）。

Arrow-key navigation for the DSH Web GUI. Switch sessions without leaving the
keyboard:

dsh-arrowkey-nav README · dsh-arrowkey-nav：| Key | Action | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `↑` | previous session | inside the current workspace |
| `↓` | next session | inside the current workspace |
| `←` | previous workspace | all workspaces |
| `→` | next workspace | all workspaces |

dsh-arrowkey-nav README · dsh-arrowkey-nav：`↑`/`↓` wrap around at the ends of the workspace and never cross into a
neighbouring one; crossing is what `←`/`→` are for. After a switch the target
row is scrolled into view, and focus returns to the composer if that is where
the press started, so typing can continue immediately.

dsh-arrowkey-nav README · Version and DSH lines：One version serves every supported host line. Version `0.5.0` is tested with
all rc releases of the DSH 0.1.0–0.2.0 lines — the exact whitelist is
`engines.dsh`, distributed from the single source `scripts/hosts.mjs` by
`scripts/sync-hosts.mjs` (hand edits fail `npm run hosts:check`):

| DSH line | tested rc releases |
| --- | --- |
| 0.1.0 | rc.2, rc.3, rc.6, rc.7, rc.8 |
| 0.1.1 | rc.1, rc.2 |
| 0.1.2 | rc.1 |
| 0.1.5 | rc.1, rc.2, rc.3 |
| 0.1.7 | rc.1, rc.2 |
| 0.2.0 | rc.1, rc.2 |

dsh-arrowkey-nav README · Version and DSH lines：- There is no per-line build: both switching generations are dispatched by
  capability probing in one bundle (`uiWorkspace.openSession` on the 0.1.6+
  generations, `sessions.open` on the older ones), so every host line runs the
  same code.
- On the 0.1.0/0.1.1 lines (`dsh-client-runtime` generation) support is
  declaration-complete and unit-tested, but real-host keystroke verification is
  still pending; until then treat those cells as best effort.

dsh-arrowkey-nav README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-arrowkey-nav -w
```

The registry's `latest` is the one version for every line. Each line also has a
dist-tag pointing at the same build — `dsh-arrowkey-nav@dsh-0.2.0`,
`dsh-arrowkey-nav@dsh-0.1.5`, and so on — if you prefer naming the line; the
install target is identical. A host release outside the table above is
rejected by the `engines.dsh` whitelist instead of mounting half-broken.

dsh-arrowkey-nav README · Install：Restart the profile afterwards — a running instance does not hot-load a new
bundle layer. Then reload `http://127.0.0.1:3080`.

Confirm the row is in the composed tree:

```sh
dsh web --dump-config | Select-String dsh-arrowkey-nav
```

A local checkout can be registered instead with
`dsh plugin --profile web add <absolute path to the checkout> -w`; see
[INSTALL.md](./INSTALL.md) for the full guide, including upgrades, verification
and removal.

dsh-arrowkey-nav README · Remove：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-arrowkey-nav
```

Restart, and the keys behave exactly as before the install: the listener is
owned by the plugin's Cordis effect and is removed with it.

dsh-arrowkey-nav README · How it works：Identity comes from the two client controllers, never from the DOM: rows carry
no `data-*` and no `id`, so a row cannot be asked what session it is.

dsh-arrowkey-nav README · How it works：- Every switch goes through the capability-probed executor: `ctx.uiWorkspace.openSession(id)`
  on the DSH 0.1.6+ generations, `ctx.sessions.open(id)` on the older lines — one
  bundle, no per-line build. The details panel needs no
  handling: the shipped frame already closes it when the current session
  changes.
- `ctx.workspaces.list.getSnapshot()` supplies the workspace order — the order
  `←`/`→` walks, and the source of each workspace's member list.

dsh-arrowkey-nav README · How it works：**Which session is "next" follows the order the sidebar is drawing**, not the
controller's member order. Those disagree in exactly the case you notice: the
sidebar reconciles its own persisted order with the membership and promotes
recently-active sessions to the top, so an old session jumps to the first row
the moment you open it. The plugin therefore reads the rendered row order out of
the sidebar, and falls back to the controller order when the sidebar is not
mounted (collapsed rail). A section is accepted only when its rows account for
every session the controller reports for that workspace; an ambiguous or
mismatched section falls back instead of guessing.

dsh-arrowkey-nav README · How it works：Keys are left alone when the event already belongs to somebody else: any
modifier, IME composition, an event already handled upstream, or a focus inside
a dialog, menu or another editable field (the sidebar's session search, a rename
box). The listener registers in the capture phase but only calls
`preventDefault()` when it actually navigates.

dsh-arrowkey-nav README · How it works：The composer is the one conditional case. An **empty composer yields its arrow
keys** — there is no caret to move, so the key is free — which is what lets you
navigate right after sending a message, while the composer still holds focus.
Once the composer **holds a draft, its arrow keys belong to the caret again**,
so editing a prompt is never hijacked.

dsh-arrowkey-nav README · How it works：The browser half has no React components, no CSS and no platform-module
requests, and the package has no runtime dependencies — `lib/client.js` is
generated by `scripts/build-client.mjs` into the module-loader contract the page
expects.

dsh-arrowkey-nav README · Development：```sh
npm run typecheck   # both compiler faces
npm test            # resolver unit tests + built-bundle smoke tests
npm run build       # regenerate lib/client.js after editing src/client
```

`npm run build` needs `typescript`; if it is not installed in this package, point
`DSH_TYPESCRIPT` at an existing `typescript` module directory.

dsh-arrowkey-nav README · Known limitations：- **A collapsed workspace group does not scroll.** Its rows are not mounted, and
  dsh exposes no public way to expand a group, so the switch happens but the
  target row stays out of sight. The workspace holding the current session is
  kept expanded by dsh itself, so `↑`/`↓` are unaffected.
- **A rail-collapsed sidebar does not scroll** for the same reason: the tree is
  not mounted. The switch still happens.
- **"In one list" mode** has no workspace sections, but `←`/`→` still walk the
  controller's workspace order, so the list may appear to jump between sections.
- **Scrolling is best effort.** Any lookup failure is swallowed: the selection
  has already moved, and a missing row must never turn into a wrong one.
- **Snapshot fields are pre-stable.** `sessions` and `workspaces` snapshot shapes are
  pre-stable — the tested host releases are exactly the `engines.dsh` whitelist
  (`engines.dsh: 0.1.0-rc.2 || 0.1.0-rc.3 || 0.1.0-rc.6 || 0.1.0-rc.7 || 0.1.0-rc.8 || 0.1.1-rc.1 || 0.1.1-rc.2 || 0.1.2-rc.1 || 0.1.5-rc.1 || 0.1.5-rc.2 || 0.1.5-rc.3 || 0.1.7-rc.1 || 0.1.7-rc.2 || 0.2.0-rc.1 || 0.2.0-rc.2 || 0.2.1-rc.1 || 0.2.1-rc.2 || 0.2.1-rc

dsh-arrowkey-nav README · Layout：```
src/index.ts                node half: loader entry, installs nothing
src/client/constants.ts     keys owned, DOM anchors read
src/client/navigate.ts      narrow waist: snapshot types + arrow resolver
src/client/apply.ts         execution: open / blank-first / connectWorkspace
